batchName: Late Republic: The Social War and Sulla (91-78 BCE) - Easy Batch 1
chapterName: Late Republic: The Social War and Sulla (91-78 BCE)

questions.question: Who were the Samnites?
options: Rome's oldest allies, living just south of the city
A Greek colony on the Bay of Naples loyal to Rome
A tough mountain people of south-central Italy long at war with Rome
A Gallic tribe settled in the Po valley of the north
questions.explanation: The Samnites were hardy mountain people who had fought Rome for generations. They were among the last rebels to keep fighting in the Social War.
questions.sourceQuote: Among them were the Samnites, a tough mountain people of south-central Italy who had fought Rome for generations.

questions.question: Which Greek city did Sulla storm and sack in 86 BC for siding with Mithridates?
options: Sparta
Athens
Thebes
Corinth
questions.explanation: Sulla sacked Athens on 1 March 86 BC. That summer he crushed huge armies of Mithridates at Chaeronea and Orchomenus.
questions.sourceQuote: On 1 March 86 BC, he stormed and sacked Athens, which had sided with Mithridates.

questions.question: What did Sulla's self-written epitaph boast?
options: He had saved Rome from both the Italians and Mithridates
He alone had given up supreme power of his own free will
He never once lost a battle in all his years of command
No friend served him and no enemy wronged him without full repayment
questions.explanation: The epitaph celebrated Sulla repaying both kindness and injury in full. Rome gave him a funeral grander than any for generations.
questions.sourceQuote: His self-written epitaph boasted that no friend had ever served him, and no enemy wronged him, without being repaid in full.

questions.question: What honour did Sulla win near Nola during the Social War?
options: The civic crown of oak leaves for saving a citizen
The title of Father of the Fatherland from the Senate
The grass crown, Rome's highest military honour
The mural crown for first scaling an enemy wall
questions.explanation: Sulla won the grass crown (corona graminea), Rome's highest military honour, near Nola. In the same campaign he also took Pompeii.
questions.sourceQuote: In the south, Sulla took Pompeii and won the grass crown (*corona graminea*), Rome's highest military honour, near Nola.

questions.question: Where was the decisive battle of Sulla's civil war fought on 1 November 82 BC?
options: The plain of Chaeronea
The Colline Gate of Rome
The Tolenus River
The port of Brundisium
questions.explanation: The Colline Gate lay on Rome's north-eastern edge. Sulla fought there against a large Samnite and Lucanian army.
questions.sourceQuote: The decisive battle came on 1 November 82 BC at the Colline Gate, on Rome's north-eastern edge, against a large Samnite and Lucanian army.

questions.question: What name did the rebel allies give to the rival state they created?
options: Latium
Samnium
Italia
Etruria
questions.explanation: The rebels called their new state Italia. It had a forum, a senate of 500 members, two consuls and twelve generals.
questions.sourceQuote: The rebels built a rival state they called Italia.

questions.question: What dangerous lesson did Sulla's career teach later Roman generals?
options: Italian allies could never be trusted with arms
A general with a loyal army could seize Rome
The Senate could always restrain its commanders
Peace with eastern kings brought the most glory
questions.explanation: Sulla's example outlasted his laws. A later general reportedly asked, "If Sulla could, why can't I?"
questions.sourceQuote: He had shown that a general with a loyal army could seize Rome, and a later general reportedly asked, "If Sulla could, why can't I?"

questions.question: As consul in 88 BC, Sulla was given command against which king?
options: Antiochus, king of Syria
Mithridates, king of Pontus
Tigranes, king of Armenia
Jugurtha, king of Numidia
questions.explanation: Mithridates ruled Pontus on the Black Sea's southern shore. He had overrun Rome's province in Asia and arranged the massacre of some 80,000 Romans and Italians.
questions.sourceQuote: The Senate gave him a rich and glorious prize: command against Mithridates, king of Pontus on the Black Sea's southern shore.

questions.question: According to the fullest surviving ancient account, why did the allies go to war with Rome?
options: They rose to free the slaves working on Roman estates
They wanted to restore the old Samnite kingdom in the mountains
They demanded Roman citizenship, were refused, and fought to win it
They wanted to stop Rome's war against Mithridates in the East
questions.explanation: The ancient narrative presents a clear story of citizenship refused and then fought for. In its words, the allies wanted to be "partners in rule rather than subjects."
questions.sourceQuote: He tells a clear story: the allies demanded Roman citizenship, were refused, and went to war to win it.

questions.question: What was a proscription under Sulla?
options: A decree confiscating all public land held by allies
A public list of men condemned to death without trial
A ban on carrying weapons inside the city of Rome
A census registering newly enfranchised Italians
questions.explanation: Anyone could kill a proscribed man and claim a reward. The first list held about 80 names, and hundreds more followed.
questions.sourceQuote: His most infamous weapon was the proscription (*proscriptio*), a public list of men condemned to death without trial.
